lockup.summary: Directors, executive officers, existing shareholders and the private placement investor have agreed not to sell for 365 days after the prospectus date, with some exceptions. The company itself has agreed to a 180-day lock-up.

what: OPay runs a mobile app for payments, loans and other financial services, mainly in Nigeria and other emerging markets.
proceeds: It plans to use the money for general corporate purposes. This includes technology, distribution, new products, market expansion, and possible acquisitions or investments in other businesses.
risks: It faces strong and growing competition in fintech, including from banks, phone companies and rivals with more money and bigger user bases.
Outages or failures in its computer systems or third-party data centres could disrupt its services and hurt its business.
Demand for its services may fall if it fails to keep up with new technology and changing customer needs.
It is growing fast but has a short operating history, which makes its future results hard to predict.
